sitter-sheet.oneLine: a one-page sheet for a babysitter or pet sitter: contacts, routines, allergies and quirks.
sitter-sheet.storesWhat: Your home address, phone numbers, backup contacts, allergies and medications, bedtime and feeding routines, and every other detail you type for the sitter
sitter-sheet.storageMechanism: in this browser's localStorage under `sitter-baby` for a babysitter sheet or `sitter-pet` for a pet sitter sheet — one key per sheet type, so the two never overwrite each other
sitter-sheet.leavesDevice: Nothing is uploaded — there is no account, no server and no analytics, and this sheet holds your address and your children's medications, so we are precise about it. A share link or QR code carries the entire sheet inside the link's own # fragment, which browsers never send to any web server, so it travels only if you copy it or show the code yourself. Anyone who has that link, or photographs that QR code, can read the whole sheet including your address. Send it directly to your sitter, the way you would hand over the paper version — not into a group chat and not anywhere public.
thirdParties: Stripe — only if you tap the tip jar, which opens buy.stripe.com in a new tab. We never see or store card details.
Firebase Hosting (Google) serves the app's static files and keeps ordinary short-lived web-server logs such as IP addresses. It cannot record your address, because it is never sent to it.
permissions: write-only clipboard access when you tap Copy link — most browsers show no prompt, and the app cannot read your clipboard
sitter-sheet.verifyTip: Turn off Wi-Fi and mobile data, reload, fill in the whole sheet and print it — every step works offline, so none of it was ever uploaded. Open DevTools → Network while you type your address and you will see no requests at all; open Application → Local Storage and you will see the single `sitter-baby` or `sitter-pet` key that holds it, on your device.

specials-planner.oneLine: a year-long lesson planner for art, music, PE and library specials teachers.
specials-planner.storesWhat: Your schedule setup and every lesson, plan and note you type
specials-planner.storageMechanism: in this browser's localStorage under the key `palette2`, with an in-memory fallback if the browser refuses to store anything — in which case the app tells you plainly rather than pretending it saved
specials-planner.leavesDevice: Nothing, as the app is currently built. The optional Google Drive save/load feature is switched off in the shipped code: the OAuth client id it depends on is empty (`const CLIENT_ID = ""` in index.html), so the Drive buttons are hidden, the Google Identity script is never loaded, and no request to Google's APIs is possible. If that feature is ever turned on, it would ask only for the narrow `drive.file` scope — files the app itself created, never the rest of your Drive and never your email — and your browser would talk to Google directly; the token would never pass through us. The app needs no student information at all; anything you do type stays here like everything else.
thirdParties: Stripe — only if you tap the tip jar, which opens buy.stripe.com in a new tab. We never see or store card details.
Firebase Hosting (Google) serves the app's static files and keeps ordinary short-lived web-server logs such as IP addresses.

Google Drive and Google Identity Services — code for an optional Drive backup exists in the page but is disabled in the shipped build (no OAuth client id), so no connection to Google's APIs is ever made. If it is ever enabled, this page will say so.
permissions: none
specials-planner.verifyTip: Turn off Wi-Fi and mobile data, reload, and plan a full week — it works, because the app is cached on your device and has nothing to call. Open DevTools → Network while you type lesson notes and you will see no requests at all. To confirm the Drive feature is genuinely off, view the page source and search for CLIENT_ID: it is set to an empty string, and every Drive function returns immediately without it.

sub-plans.storageMechanism: in this browser's localStorage under the key `subplans`, with your grade band under `subplans.band` and the print-a-QR preference under `subplans.qrpaper`
sub-plans.leavesDevice: Nothing is uploaded — there is no account, no server, no analytics and nothing to opt out of. The one exception is a share link, and only if you copy it yourself: Copy link packs the whole folder into the link's own # fragment, which browsers never send to any web server. Nothing is stored anywhere — the link IS the folder. team-parent.oneLine: a season of practices, games, snack duty and carpools in one link every family can open.
team-parent.storesWhat: The team page's title and description, every practice, game and duty slot with its label and capacity, the name each family types when they RSVP or claim a duty, and any announcements or notes posted
team-parent.storageMechanism: in Google Firestore, under the Firebase project `sws-apps-9646d`, and mirrored into this browser's IndexedDB offline cache so the schedule still opens at a field with no signal. This browser separately holds the display name you last used under `tp-myname`, and — only if the organiser signs in by email link — that email address under `tp-signin-email`
team-parent.leavesDevice: Everything on a team page is stored on Google's Firestore servers, because that is the only way every family sees the same schedule update live. This app therefore does not carry the 'nothing leaves your device' promise the rest of the portfolio makes. Concretely: the page title and description, every slot label, every claimant name (capped at 60 characters) and every announcement body (capped at 2000) are written to Firestore and readable by anyone holding the 6-character share link. Only the organiser signs in — anonymously by default, or with Google or an email link if they choose; families need no account and are signed in anonymously behind the scenes so the app can tell one RSVP from another. Separately, an address you type into a location field is turned into an ordinary Google Maps link: nothing is fetched, and you only go there if you tap it.
thirdParties: Google Firebase Firestore (firestore.googleapis.com) — stores every team page, slot and RSVP.
Google Firebase Authentication (identitytoolkit.googleapis.com) — issues the anonymous or signed-in user id attached to RSVPs.
Google gstatic.com — the Firebase SDK modules are fetched from https://www.gstatic.com/firebasejs/12.17.1/ on the first visit, then cached by the service worker.
Google Sign-In (accounts.google.com) — only if the organiser chooses 'Sign in with Google' instead of staying anonymous.
Google Maps — a typed address becomes a plain link; tapping it navigates you to google.com/maps with that address in the URL. Nothing is fetched unless you tap.
Stripe — only if you tap the tip jar, which opens buy.stripe.com in a new tab. We never see or store card details.
Firebase Hosting (Google) serves the app's static files and keeps ordinary short-lived web-server logs such as IP addresses.
permissions: write-only clipboard access when you tap Copy link — most browsers show no prompt, and the app cannot read your clipboard
team-parent.verifyTip: Open DevTools → Network and load the page: you will see the Firebase SDK fetched from gstatic.com and nothing else. Open a team page and you will see requests to firestore.googleapis.com — that is the shared schedule, and it is the only thing sent. There is no analytics call: apps/team-parent/firebase-config.js contains no measurementId, so Google Analytics is never initialised.

wheel-picker.oneLine: a fair spinning wheel for picking names, chores or winners.
wheel-picker.storageMechanism: inside this page's own URL # fragment, which is why bookmarking or sharing the link keeps the wheel forever — the only thing ever written to localStorage is your chosen spin length, under the key `wheel.spin`, and the spin history is held in memory alone and disappears when you close the tab
wheel-picker.leavesDevice: Nothing. The wheel lives in the link's # fragment, and browsers never send a # fragment to any web server, so the names travel only if you paste that link somewhere yourself — and anyone who has the link sees the same list. The spin history exists purely so you can point at it when somebody says the wheel was rigged; it is never recorded anywhere off this device and there is no record kept of who won.
thirdParties: Stripe — only if you tap the tip jar, which opens buy.stripe.com in a new tab. We never see or store card details.
Firebase Hosting (Google) serves the app's static files and keeps ordinary short-lived web-server logs such as IP addresses.

wheel-picker.verifyTip: Turn off Wi-Fi and mobile data, reload and spin — it works, because the whole wheel is in the address bar in front of you. Watch the URL change as you add names: that is the entire storage and sharing mechanism, and there is nothing else. Open DevTools → Network while you spin and you will see no requests at all.

grade-sheet.oneLine: a private gradebook a teacher keeps on her own computer — rosters, marks, averages and printouts.
grade-sheet.storesWhat: Your class names and periods, every student name (or initials, or ID) you paste or type, every assignment and its points, every mark, missing/excused flag, absence flag and note you record, and your grading settings
grade-sheet.storageMechanism: in this browser's own IndexedDB database `sws-gradesheet` — an object store `classes` holding one record per class with that class's whole roster, assignments and marks; `meta` holding a single `book` record with your settings and a class index; and `files` for a backup file handle. The only localStorage key it writes is `sws.gradesheet.seen`, which holds a date and is used to notice that this browser has erased your data
grade-sheet.leavesDevice: Nothing. There is no network code of any kind in the app — no fetch, no upload, no analytics endpoint, no update check, no font fetched from anywhere. The only copies that ever exist elsewhere are the backup file and CSV you save yourself, and anything you print.
thirdParties: Firebase Hosting (Google) serves the app's static files and keeps ordinary short-lived web-server logs such as IP addresses. It cannot record anything you enter, because nothing you enter is ever sent to it.
permissions: No camera, microphone or location. Saving a backup uses an ordinary browser download.
grade-sheet.verifyTip: Turn off Wi-Fi, reload the page and keep marking — entry, averages, printing and export all still work, because the whole app is cached on your device by its service worker. An app that runs with the network off is an app that cannot be sending your students' grades anywhere. To look directly, open DevTools → Application → IndexedDB → sws-gradesheet and read every record the app holds; or press Ctrl+U and search the source for the word fetch. There is not one.
